sections.html:
Hallandale Beach is a compact, oddly shaped city at the southern tip of Broward County. Its outline goes back to a 1947 deal that allowed annexation from Federal Highway east to the ocean, with the oceanfront north of Beach Boulevard going to Hollywood. The city covers 4.55 square miles, 4.21 of them land.

A 2020 headcount found 41,217 people in 17,573 households. Homes are packed close together here, so before you tell a buyer what could be built or added, ask the city which zoning and redevelopment rules apply to your parcel.

The Building Division offers two websites. ePermitsOneStop is shared by the city and Broward County, so plans get reviewed by both at once. HB Self-Service is where you pay fees, check on a permit and book inspections. Searching by address or parcel brings up permit history, and no account is needed.

Run that search on your own house before listing. Any permit that never reached a final inspection should be closed, and the Building Division can explain how. Roofs, windows, electrical work and balcony enclosures are what buyers' inspectors chase most. This city took direct hits from the 1926 hurricane and from Hurricane Katrina in August 2005, so older homes often draw questions about roofs, windows and past claims. Keep claim paperwork next to the permit list.

Broward County Records, Taxes and Treasury sends the bill and supports the Value Adjustment Board, the body that hears disputes over exemptions, classifications and values. Visit the Recording Office at 115 S. Andrews Ave, Room 114, Fort Lauderdale, or call 954-831-4000 or 3-1-1 between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. The Value Adjustment Board sits at 1801 NW 49th Street, Fort Lauderdale.

How the Florida tax year runs for a Broward owner
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value is set
March 1Exemption applications due
AugustProposed tax notice mailed; a challenge goes to the clerk within 25 days
November to FebruaryBills arrive; early-payment discount steps down from 4 percent to 1 percent
April 1Unpaid taxes turn delinquent
By June 1Tax certificates sold

• Homestead: the first $25,000 reduces all taxes, and a further layer of up to $25,000 reduces non-school taxes on assessed value above $50,000.
  • Save Our Homes: assessed value may climb each year by the lower of 3 percent or the inflation change, and it resets by itself when the home sells.
  • Renting: the exemption stops once the unit is leased or no longer your permanent home.
  • Portability: the benefit can move with you to a new Florida homestead, provided you set that up within three years.

When you sell, your cap goes away. The Broward Property Appraiser can tell you how the parcel will be reassessed for a buyer, and the new owner's bill will likely be higher than yours. Buyers who estimate their own taxes can land far from your current figure, so hand them your tax history up front.

Ordinance No. 96-25, dated December 27, 1996, created the Hallandale Beach Community Redevelopment Agency. The district stretches from Pembroke Road in the north to the Dade-Broward County line in the south, and from Interstate 95 in the west to NE 14th Avenue and its canal in the east.

A house inside those lines may be affected by a redevelopment plan. Phone the city's planning staff and learn what a future owner may build. Such plans can touch park access, traffic and nearby streets, and having an answer ready helps a buyer feel comfortable.

sections.h2: Documentary stamps and other closing costs
sections.html:
Broward charges the regular doc stamp rate of 70 cents for each $100 of consideration, due to the clerk when the deed is recorded. Miami-Dade's higher rate and surtax stay out of the picture. Buyer and seller are both liable to the state, whatever the contract says about who pays.

Recording fees follow section 28.24 and are counted by the page. Condominium and homeowners associations must provide an estoppel or payoff letter, which can add days before closing. Ask for it the moment you have a buyer.

A tenant in the house changes your schedule. A month-to-month tenancy ends on 30 days' notice, and a 3-day notice starts the process for unpaid rent. Once a landlord wins in court, the sheriff posts a 24-hour notice and then puts the landlord in possession.

When an owner has died, summary administration may fit a small estate: the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or the decedent has been gone more than two years. A foreclosure sale lands 20 to 35 days after judgment. Your closing agent or a Florida attorney can say which path matches your situation.

If the value on your proposed tax notice looks too high, you have 25 days from the mailing to file a petition with the clerk. The Broward Value Adjustment Board hears these cases at 1801 NW 49th Street, Fort Lauderdale. Questions can go to 954-357-7205 or 954-357-5444.

Do this before you sell, since a lower assessment helps you through proration and helps your buyer see a fair history. Bring the notice, recent sale prices near you and photos of any condition problems.

Whatever value ends up on the roll, the tax collector bills from it in November, and your closing agent prorates that bill between you and the buyer as usual.

A cash buyer does not need a lender's appraisal or loan underwriting, so the usual wait for a bank's sign-off disappears. Repairs are priced into the offer instead of negotiated after an inspection, and you do not host open houses. Title work, payoff letters, association paperwork and recording still take days, so ask for a written timeline and a named closing agent.

If the house has open permits or a lien, tell the buyer at the start. A lender-financed buyer may insist on fixing those first, while a cash buyer can often close with them open and handle the cleanup after, which is worth comparing against what a listing would net after repairs.

sections.h2: What to gather before you take offers
sections.html:
Start with records: the deed, the latest tax bill, the permit history, and loan payoff details. A condo or HOA home also needs the association paperwork. Then compare routes. An agent listing draws the most showings, a cash buyer can drop lender conditions, and a private sale leaves the paperwork to you.

With any route, insist on terms in writing and a date when funds reach you. Afterward your closing agent drafts the deed, collects the stamp tax, files with the clerk, and divides the year's property tax between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Which county is Hallandale Beach in?
faqs.a: Broward County. The area belonged to Dade County until Broward was formed in 1915.

faqs.q: Do I pay documentary stamp tax in Broward?
faqs.a: Yes. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration on the deed, and the clerk collects it at recording. Miami-Dade's rate does not apply.

faqs.q: How do I check my permit history?
faqs.a: Open the HB Self-Service portal and search by address, parcel number or inspection number. Finalized documents can be viewed with no account.

faqs.q: Where do I file a property value challenge?
faqs.a: File a petition with the clerk within 25 days of the proposed tax notice. The Broward Value Adjustment Board hears it, and 954-357-7205 or 954-357-5444 can answer questions.

faqs.q: How much notice does a month-to-month tenant get?
faqs.a: 30 days. For unpaid rent, a landlord starts with a 3-day notice.
